64832-the-steam-fire-engine-and-the-old-.title: The Steam Fire Engine And The Old Time Fire Bell
64832-the-steam-fire-engine-and-the-old-.creator: Unknown
64832-the-steam-fire-engine-and-the-old-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. England deserves the credit for invention of the steam fire engine, but to America goes the distinction of having perfected it. Nowhere was the steam fire engine more widely used than in the United States, with its preponderance of highly inflammable wooden buildings. Certainly nowhere else were the caretakers of the glittering engines so zealous in exhibiting their machines’ amazing qualities at every opportunity.

arxiv-1807-04485.title: Predicting Usefulness of Code Review Comments using Textual Features and Developer Experience
arxiv-1807-04485.creator: Mohammad Masudur Rahman Chanchal K. Roy § Raula G. Kula
arxiv-1807-04485.description: Abstract Although peer code review is widely adopted in both commercial and open source development, existing studies suggest that such code reviews often contain a significant amount of non-useful review comments. Unfortunately, to date, no tools or techniques exist that can provide automatic support in improving those non-useful comments.

arxiv-1812-07631.title: K ​ 2 K2 Ultracool Dwarfs Survey. V. High superflare rates on rapidly rotating late-M dwarfs 2018 K ​ 2 K2 Ultracool Dwarfs Survey. V. High superflare rates on rapidly rotating late-M dwarfs – References
arxiv-1812-07631.creator: R. R. Paudel, J. E. Gizis, D. J. Mullan, S. J. Schmidt, A. J. Burgasser, P. K. G. Williams, A. Youngblood
arxiv-1812-07631.description: Abstract We observed strong superflares (defined as flares with energy in excess of 10 33 erg) on three late-M dwarfs: 2MASS J08315742+2042213 (hereafter 2M0831+2042; M7 V), 2MASS J08371832+2050349 (hereafter 2M0837+2050; M8 V) and 2MASS J08312608+2244586 (hereafter 2M0831+2244; M9 V). 2M0831+2042 and 2M0837+2050 are members of the young ( ∼ \sim 700 Myr) open cluster Praesepe.

arxiv-1904-06562.title: Tensorization of the strong data processing inequality for quantum chi-square divergences
arxiv-1904-06562.creator: Yu Cao, Jianfeng Lu
arxiv-1904-06562.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Yu Cao, Jianfeng Lu. It is well-known that any quantum channel ℰ \mathcal{E} satisfies the data processing inequality (DPI), with respect to various divergences, e.g., quantum χ κ 2 \chi^{2}_{\kappa} divergences and quantum relative entropy. More specifically, the data processing inequality states that the divergence between two arbitrary quantum states ρ \rho and σ \sigma does not increase under the action of any quantum channel ℰ \mathcal{E} .

arxiv-2102-06921.title: Polarization inhibits the phase transition of Axelrod’s model
arxiv-2102-06921.creator: Carlos Gracia-Lázaro, Edgardo Brigatti, Alexis R. Hernández, Yamir Moreno
arxiv-2102-06921.description: Abstract We study the effect of polarization in Axelrod’s model of cultural dissemination. This is done through the introduction of a cultural feature that takes only two values, while the other features can present a larger number of possible traits.

arxiv-2108-12544.title: Construction for both self-dual codes and LCD codes
arxiv-2108-12544.creator: Keita Ishizuka, Ken Saito
arxiv-2108-12544.description: Abstract From a given [ n , k ] [n,k] code C C , we give a method for constructing many [ n , k ] [n,k] codes C ′ C^{\prime} such that the hull dimensions of C C and C ′ C^{\prime} are identical.

arxiv-2109-05862.title: Random-time quantum measurements
arxiv-2109-05862.creator: Markus Sifft, Daniel Hägele
arxiv-2109-05862.description: Abstract The analysis of a continuous measurement record z ⁡ ( t ) z(t) poses a fundamental challenge in quantum measurement theory. Different approaches have been used in the past as records can, e.g., exhibit predominantly Gaussian noise, telegraph noise, or clicks at random times.

arxiv-2112-03459.title: A Novel Convergence Analysis for Algorithms of the Adam Family
arxiv-2112-03459.creator: Zhishuai Guo †, Yi Xu ‡, Wotao Yin ‡, Rong Jin ‡, Tianbao Yang †
arxiv-2112-03459.description: Abstract Since its invention in 2014, the Adam optimizer ( Kingma and Ba 2014 ) has received tremendous attention. On one hand, it has been widely used in deep learning and many variants have been proposed, while on the other hand their theoretical convergence property remains to be a mystery.

arxiv-2206-03514.title: Constraining the Size of the Circumgalactic Medium Using the Transverse Autocorrelation Function of C IV Absorbers in Paired Quasar Spectra ESIRedux (Prochaska et al. 2003), MASE pipeline (Bochanski et al. 2009), linetools (Prochaska et al. 2016), PypeIt (Prochaska et al. 2020)
arxiv-2206-03514.creator: Abby Mintz, Marc Rafelski, Regina A. Jorgenson, Michele Fumagalli, Rajeshwari Dutta, Crystal L. Martin, Elisabeta Lusso, Kate H. R. Rubin, John M. O’Meara
arxiv-2206-03514.description: Abstract The circumgalactic medium (CGM) plays a vital role in the formation and evolution of galaxies, acting as a lifeline between galaxies and the surrounding intergalactic medium (IGM). In this study we leverage a unique sample of quasar pairs to investigate the properties of the CGM with absorption line tomography.

arxiv-2304-05810.title: Diversity of early kilonova with the realistic opacities of highly ionized heavy elements
arxiv-2304-05810.creator: Smaranika Banerjee, Masaomi Tanaka, Daiji Kato, Gediminas Gaigalas
arxiv-2304-05810.description: Abstract We investigate the early ( t < 1 t<1 day) kilonova from the neutron star merger by deriving atomic opacities for all the elements from La to Ra ( Z = 57 − 88 Z=57-88 ) ionized to the states V - XI. The opacities at high temperatures for the elements with open f f -shells (e.g.

arxiv-2402-16921.title: Sparse2Inverse: Self-supervised inversion of sparse-view CT data
arxiv-2402-16921.creator: Nadja Gruber Johannes Schwab Elke Gizewski Markus Haltmeier
arxiv-2402-16921.description: Abstract Sparse-view computed tomography (CT) enables fast and low-dose CT imaging, an essential feature for patient-save medical imaging and rapid non-destructive testing. In sparse-view CT, only a few projection views are acquired, causing standard reconstructions to suffer from severe artifacts and noise. To address these issues, we propose a self-supervised image reconstruction strategy.

arxiv-2406-15973.title: Performance of plastic scintillator modules for top veto tracker at Taishan Antineutrino Observatory
arxiv-2406-15973.creator: Guang Luo, Xiaohao Yin, Fengpeng An, Zhimin Wang, Y.K.Hor, Peizhi Lu, Ruhui Li, Yichen Li, Wei He, Wei Wang, Xiang Xiao
arxiv-2406-15973.description: Abstract The Taishan Antineutrino Observatory (TAO) experiment incorporates a top veto tracker (TVT) system comprising 160 modules, each composed of plastic scintillator (PS) strips, embedded wavelength shifting fibers (WLS-fibers), and silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs). This article highlights the performance of all produced modules following the production and readout/trigger design, providing insights for scintillation detectors with WLS-fibers.

arxiv-2407-15411.title: Scalable Dynamic Embedding Size Search for Streaming Recommendation
arxiv-2407-15411.creator: Yunke Qu, Liang Qu, Tong Chen, Xiangyu Zhao, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Hongzhi Yin
arxiv-2407-15411.description: Abstract . Recommender systems typically represent users and items by learning their embeddings, which are usually set to uniform dimensions and dominate the model parameters. However, real-world recommender systems often operate in streaming recommendation scenarios, where the number of users and items continues to grow, leading to substantial storage resource consumption for these embeddings.

arxiv-2505-00775.title: Characterizing the Radiative-Convective Structure of Dense Rocky Planet Atmospheres
arxiv-2505-00775.creator: Jessica Cmiel, Robin Wordsworth, Jacob T. Seeley
arxiv-2505-00775.description: Abstract We use a one-dimensional line-by-line radiative-convective model to simulate hot, dense terrestrial-planet atmospheres. We find that strong shortwave absorption by H 2 ​ O \text{H}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\vphantom{\text{2}}\smash[t]{\text{2}}}^{\vphantom{\smash[t]{\text{2}}}\hphantom{\text{2}}\text{}}\text{O} and CO 2 \text{CO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\vphantom{\text{2}}\smash[t]{\text{2}}}^{\vphantom{\smash[t]{\text{2}}}\hphantom{\text{2}}\text{}} inhibits near-surface convection, reducing surface temperatures by up to ∼ 2000 \sim\!2000 K compared to fully convective predictions.

arxiv-2507-13496.title: Growing Sparse Quantum Codes from a Seed
arxiv-2507-13496.creator: ChunJun Cao, Brad Lackey
arxiv-2507-13496.description: Abstract It is generally unclear whether smaller codes can be “concatenated” to systematically create quantum LDPC codes or their sparse subsystem code cousins where the degree of the Tanner graph remains bounded while increasing the code distance. In this work, we use a slight generalization of concatenation called conjoining introduced by the quantum lego formalism.

arxiv-2507-22315.title: Monopole Traps for Position-Based Information Coding
arxiv-2507-22315.creator: Prakash Timsina, Andres Chappa, Deema Alyones, Boris Kiefer, Ludi Miao*
arxiv-2507-22315.description: Abstract We propose a spin-ice-based heterostructure capable of encoding magnetic monopole quasiparticle positions for non-volatile information storage applications. Building upon two-dimensional magnetic monopole gases formed at the interface between 2-in–2-out spin ice and all-in–all-out antiferromagnetic pyrochlore iridate, the design introduces a 3-in-1-out/1-in-3-out fragmented barrier layer into the spin-ice matrix, defining two energetically stable monopole traps.

arxiv-2511-07470.title: Slimmable NAM: Neural Amp Models with adjustable runtime computational cost
arxiv-2511-07470.creator: Steven Atkinson
arxiv-2511-07470.description: Abstract This work demonstrates “slimmable Neural Amp Models”, whose size and computational cost can be changed without additional training and with negligible computational overhead, enabling musicians to easily trade off between the accuracy and compute of the models they are using.

arxiv-2511-13530.title: Towards Affect-Adaptive Human-Robot Interaction: A Protocol for Multimodal Dataset Collection on Social Anxiety
arxiv-2511-13530.creator: Vesna Poprcova, Iulia Lefter, Matthias Wieser, Martijn Warnier, Frances Brazier
arxiv-2511-13530.description: Abstract Social anxiety is a prevalent condition that affects interpersonal interactions and social functioning. Recent advances in artificial intelligence and social robotics offer new opportunities to examine social anxiety in the human-robot interaction context. Accurate detection of affective states and behaviours associated with social anxiety requires multimodal datasets, where each signal modality provides complementary insights into its manifestations.

arxiv-2606-30189.title: DAIN: Dynamic Agent-Based Interaction Network for Efficient and Collaborative Multimodal Reasoning

britannica-1911-fellows-sir-charles.title: Fellows, Sir Charles (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-fellows-sir-charles.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-fellows-sir-charles.description: Article 'Fellows, Sir Charles' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 10), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was born in August 1799 at Nottingham, where his family had an estate. When fourteen he drew sketches to illustrate a trip to the ruins of Newstead Abbey, which afterwards appeared on the title-page of Moore’s Life of Lord Byron. In 1820 he settled in London, where he became an active member of the British Association.

pmc-10670222.title: The Potential of Lifestyle Medicine: Strategies to Optimize Health and Well-Being in Oncology Care with Dr. Amy Comander
pmc-10670222.creator: Harshal Chorya, Helena S. Coloma, Viviana Cortiana, Muskan Joshi, Gayathri P. Menon, Maduri Balasubramanian, Chandler H. Park, Yan Leyfman
pmc-10670222.description: Simple SummaryThis collection of discussions by an experienced speaker explores the evolving landscape of lifestyle medicine in the context of cancer care and survivorship. Emphasizing the critical role of lifestyle modifications, the discussions address challenges and opportunities in optimizing cancer survivors’ health and mitigating late effects in pediatric populations.

pmc-10707872.title: Intelligent Protein Design and Molecular Characterization Techniques: A Comprehensive Review
pmc-10707872.creator: Jingjing Wang, Chang Chen, Ge Yao, Junjie Ding, Liangliang Wang, Hui Jiang, Benevides C Pessela
pmc-10707872.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In recent years, the widespread application of artificial intelligence algorithms in protein structure, function prediction, and de novo protein design has significantly accelerated the process of intelligent protein design and led to many noteworthy achievements. This advancement in protein intelligent design holds great potential to accelerate the development of new drugs, enhance the efficiency of biocatalysts, and even create entirely new biomaterials. Protein characterization is the key to the performance of intelligent protein design.

pmc-11324144.title: Approach in inputs & outputs selection of Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) efficiency measurement in hospitals: A systematic review
pmc-11324144.creator: M. Zulfakhar Zubir, A. Azimatun Noor, A. M. Mohd Rizal, A. Aziz Harith, M. Ihsanuddin Abas, Zuriyati Zakaria, Anwar Fazal A. Bakar, André Ramalho, André Ramalho, André Ramalho, André Ramalho
pmc-11324144.description: The efficiency and productivity evaluation process commonly employs Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) as a performance tool in numerous fields, such as the healthcare industry (hospitals). Therefore, this review examined various hospital-based DEA articles involving input and output variable selection approaches and the recent DEA developments.

pmc-11352949.title: Unveil Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma Heterogeneity through the Lens of Omics and Multi-Omics Approaches
pmc-11352949.creator: Veronica Porreca, Cristina Barbagallo, Eleonora Corbella, Marco Peres, Michele Stella, Giuseppina Mignogna, Bruno Maras, Marco Ragusa, Carmine Mancone, Dania Cioni
pmc-11352949.description: Simple SummaryIntrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is a highly aggressive primary liver cancer leading to death in 10–15% of cases. In recent years, the iCCA worldwide incidence has been increasing, and research is currently focused on identifying valuable diagnostic biomarkers and developing specific therapies to counteract the disease despite its high heterogeneity.

pmc-11546850.title: Comprehensive Analysis and Verification of the Prognostic Significance of Cuproptosis-Related Genes in Colon Adenocarcinoma
pmc-11546850.creator: Yixiao Gu, Chengze Li, Yinan Yan, Jingmei Ming, Yuanhua Li, Xiang Chao, Tieshan Wang, Maria Mesuraca, Maria Concetta Faniello
pmc-11546850.description: Colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) is a frequently occurring and lethal cancer. Cuproptosis is an emerging type of cell death, and the underlying pathways involved in this process in COAD remain poorly understood. Transcriptomic and clinical data for COAD patients were collected from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) databases.

pmc-11710437.title: Deciphering spatial microglial diversity in the brain of Alzheimer’s disease patients
pmc-11710437.creator: Paula Sanchez‐Molina, Dillon Brownell, Aditya Pratapa, Nadezhda Nikulina, Bassem Ben Cheikh, Jasmine Singh, Alina Bogachuk, Aude Chiot, Gregory Chin, Katie Emberley, Andrea Crotti, Randall Woltjer, Fabian Svara, Oliver Braubach, Bahareh Ajami
pmc-11710437.description: BackgroundSingle‐cell technologies have revealed significant microglial cell heterogeneity across the human brain in both health and disease. However, the integration of high‐plex protein and spatial information in single‐cell approaches constitutes a challenge essential for advancing our cell biology comprehension in the neuroscience field.

pmc-12454538.title: Population Exposure–Response Efficacy Analysis of Elranatamab (PF-06863135) in Patients with Multiple Myeloma
pmc-12454538.creator: Hoi-Kei Lon, Jennifer Hibma, Sibo Jiang, Sharon Sullivan, Erik Vandendries, Athanasia Skoura, Diane Wang, Mohamed Elmeliegy
pmc-12454538.description: BackgroundElranatamab is a heterodimeric humanized full-length bispecific antibody composed of one B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) binding arm and one cluster of differentiation 3 (CD3) binding arm. Results from the MagnetisMM-3 study indicated deep and durable responses in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM).ObjectiveThe current analysis was conducted to characterize the relationship between free (i.e.

pmc-12584433.title: Effects of cabozantinib on plasma adrenocorticotropic hormone and serum cortisol levels in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma: a retrospective study
pmc-12584433.creator: Yuji Hataya, Mayuka Kurata, Kimiaki Murabe, Takuro Hakata, Kanta Fujimoto, Toshio Iwakura, Toshinari Yamasaki, Naoki Matsuoka
pmc-12584433.description: BackgroundTyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are widely used to treat various solid tumors; however, adverse events, such as fatigue and anorexia, remain significant concerns. TKI-induced primary adrenal insufficiency (PAI) is a potential cause of these symptoms; however, its pathophysiology remains unclear. To better understand TKI-induced PAI, we conducted a retrospective study to investigate the effects of TKI on adrenocortical function.

pmc-12665882.title: A Novel Coprecipitation Path to a High‐Performing Ni/MgO Catalyst for Carbon Dioxide Methanation
pmc-12665882.creator: Anna Wolf, Michael Chumakovski, Hauke Rohr, Patrik Hauberg, Morteza Saedi, Sebastian Mangelsen, Malte Behrens
pmc-12665882.description: The novel crystalline bimetallic single‐source precursor (Ni1–x Mg x )12(CO3)8(OH)6O · y H2O with x = 0–0.5 can be converted into a highly active Ni/MgO CO2 methanation catalyst. All stages of preparation, namely, coprecipitation, crystallization, calcination, and reduction, as well as the spent catalysts have been comprehensively analyzed using powder X‐ray diffraction, physisorption, transmission electron microscopy, and other techniques.

pmc-13112369.title: Triple-negative breast cancer, pregnancy, and HLA alloreactivity: a cause for concern?
pmc-13112369.creator: Giovanna Crestani Morassutti, Maurizio Zanetti
pmc-13112369.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains the most aggressive form of breast cancer in women worldwide, with an incidence that varies considerably depending on genetic background and ethnicity. Since parity is a known risk for TNBC, here we propose that in HLA alloreactivity resulting from immunization against paternal antigens expressed by the fetus, 50% fetus–mother HLA dissimilarity in natural pregnancy and 100% fetus–mother HLA dissimilarity in surrogate motherhood, may be a risk factor in women with predisposing genetic background and ethnicity due to

pmc-13146294.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A894 EFFICIENCY AND SAFETY OF TENECTEPLASE VERSUS ALTEPLASE ACROSS DIFFERENT TREATMENT TIME WINDOWS: A MONOCENTRIC ONE-YEAR STROKE CENTER EXPERIENCE
pmc-13146294.creator: Alexander Sekita, Kosmas MacHa, Ludwig Singer, Stefan Schwab, Stefan T Gerner
pmc-13146294.description: Background and aimsTenecteplase (TNK) offers pharmacological advantages over alteplase (rt-PA) and is increasingly used for intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Our stroke center switched from rt-PA to TNK in June 2024, enabling a real-world comparison of treatment efficiency and safety across conventional, extended treatment, and other off-label scenarios.

pmc-13280060.title: Survey Dataset Supporting Blue Circular Economy Strategies for Bivalve Shell Waste Valorisation
pmc-13280060.creator: Poliana Bellei, Fernanda Caroline Magalhães, Maria Paula Mendes, Rui Vasco Silva, Manuel Francisco Costa Pereira, Ana Paula Soares Dias, Marte Jenssen, Runar Gjerp Solstad, Mahdi Kioumarsi, Inês Flores-Colen
pmc-13280060.description: The circular economy advocates for a fundamental shift, focusing on the reuse, recycling, and valorization of waste to keep materials in use for as long as possible, thereby reducing the need for new resources and minimizing waste. In this context, the concept of the Blue Circular Economy emerges, emphasizing the preservation and sustainable use of marine and coastal resources.

pmc-13398923.title: PlantRG: A Comprehensive and User‐Friendly Database for Plant Resistance Gene Analogs (RGAs)
pmc-13398923.creator: Jinghua He, Xiao Ma, Rui Cao, Zhuo Liu, Chenhao Zhang, Wei Chen, Lusheng Guo, Zipeng Meng, Rong Zhou, Xiaoming Song
pmc-13398923.description: Resistance genes are critical for plant defence against biotic stresses, and building a comprehensive, integrated data resource platform for these genes holds great significance for plant research and agriculture. Here, we developed PlantRG (http://plantrg.bio2db.com), a user‐friendly plant resistance gene database, which is built on 2 163 397 resistance genes identified from 1062 plant species.
